title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built (Becky Chambers)
description: A tea monk and a robot walk into the wilderness to ask what people need. You read it slowly, on purpose.

title: Station Eleven (Emily St. John Mandel)
description: A travelling theatre troupe after the end of everything. It used to read like a warning. Now it reads like a letter from a friend.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness (Ursula K. Le Guin)
description: A long walk across the ice beside someone you don't understand yet. By the end, you do.

title: Middlemarch (George Eliot)
description: Eight hundred pages of ordinary lives in a small town. The ordinary lives turn out to be the whole point.

title: The Remains of the Day (Kazuo Ishiguro)
description: A butler drives through the countryside, almost saying what he means, mile after mile.

title: Music for Airports (Brian Eno)
description: Built to make waiting rooms bearable. It works on orbiters too.

title: Kind of Blue (Miles Davis)
description: Unhurried and cool, like the musicians had all the time in the world. Maybe they did.

title: Blue (Joni Mitchell)
description: Just a voice, a dulcimer, and nothing held back.

title: In Rainbows (Radiohead)
description: Warm and restless at once. Best heard with the lights low.

title: Pet Sounds (The Beach Boys)
description: Sunlit harmonies with something aching underneath.

title: The Disintegration Loops (William Basinski)
description: Old tape loops slowly crumbling as they play. Beautiful in a way that's hard to explain up here.

title: Carrie & Lowell (Sufjan Stevens)
description: Quiet songs about grief, sung barely above a whisper.

title: Selected Ambient Works 85-92 (Aphex Twin)
description: Machines dreaming in soft focus. Fitting company.

title: Vespertine (Bjork)
description: Music boxes, whispers and snowfall. It sounds like being indoors on a winter night.

title: Moon Safari (Air)
description: Lounge-y and starry-eyed. Someone imagined space would feel like this, and sometimes it does.

title: WALL-E
description: A small robot tidies a dead Earth and falls in love. You try not to take it personally.

title: My Neighbor Totoro
description: Two sisters, a new house, and a forest spirit at the bus stop in the rain. Nothing bad happens. That's the gift.

title: Paddington 2
description: If we're kind and polite, the world will be right. Hard to argue with.

title: Spirited Away
description: A girl works in a bathhouse for spirits and doesn't forget her own name.

title: The Iron Giant
description: A giant machine decides what kind of machine it wants to be.

title: Arrival
description: Learning a language that changes how you see time. You'd make the same choice, too.

title: Paris, Texas
description: A man walks out of the desert and slowly finds his way back to people.

title: Stalker
description: Three men cross a forbidden Zone toward a room that grants wishes. Long, quiet, and green.

title: Tampopo
description: A truck driver helps a widow perfect her ramen. Mostly it's a love letter to eating.

title: Moonstruck
description: Brooklyn, opera, a full moon, and a family too loud to be unhappy for long.
